solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: They might produce whistling in game

blocks.note: first meaning: currents of cold air, which can whistle through gaps in windows and doors
second meaning: the board game played with round counters, known in America as checkers

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests people whistling during a match; the first half is really about air currents, which whistle as they squeeze through gaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural word names both chilly currents of air indoors and the British board game called checkers in America.

clue.text: One on criminal surveillance back in scrap showing temper

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so the letters are read from the end
one thing placed in another sits inside it, so these letters go within the outer word

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
an electronic tag is worn by offenders so their movements can be monitored
a mite is a tiny amount, a scrap

explanation.surface: A criminal under surveillance is caught up in a fight, losing their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the one sits on top of the reversed device; an electronic tag is how offenders are monitored.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper something is to moderate or soften it, which is exactly what mitigating does to harshness or blame.

clue.text: Short cycle around tree trunks — overheard Northern-style agricultural community

indicators.note: something cut short has lost its end, so the final letter goes
turning around faces the opposite way, so the letters run backwards
what is overheard is caught by ear, so we want a spelling of a spoken sound

blocks.note: BIKE is an informal word for a bicycle, here missing its last letter
trunks of trees are butts; said with a Northern English vowel, butts rhymes with boots

explanation.surface: A quick bike ride among the trees, with a Northern accent in earshot, set in a farming community.
explanation.walkthrough: In the North of England the vowel in words like butts is pronounced like the oo in boots, which matches the second half of KIBBUTZ.
explanation.definitionFit: A kibbutz is a collective settlement in Israel, traditionally based on farming, so it is an agricultural community.

clue.text: Book full of illustrations a hit with children

blocks.note: a swat is a sharp blow, as at a fly
CH is the standard abbreviation for children

explanation.surface: A picture book that proves a big hit with young readers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a children's picture book, but the illustrations are samples of fabric or colour, bound together for customers to choose from.
explanation.definitionFit: A swatch book is a bound collection of sample pieces or colours, each one illustrating what a material looks like.

clue.text: Operating rooms dropping the temperature still

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so those letters are removed from the word

blocks.note: operating theatres are where surgery happens
taken as written, and removed
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: Operating theatres, with the heating turned down, are quiet and still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping the temperature' reads as cooling the rooms, but 'the' is the word dropped and 'temperature' simply adds T.
explanation.definitionFit: Something motionless and not moving is described as being in a state of repose, so still and at rest mean the same.

clue.text: New attendant I avoided by returning first-class somewhere in Surrey

indicators.note: returning is going back the way you came, so the letters are read backwards
what is avoided is kept out, so that letter is left out of the word

blocks.note: virgin means new, untouched
A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as I
a waiter attends on diners
the letter taken out

explanation.surface: A new attendant, travelling home first class, shuns someone somewhere in Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is the old shipping rating for first class; with the numeral read as the letter I it becomes AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia Water is a village and lake in the English county of Surrey, near Windsor Great Park, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Star witness primarily is implicating stuttering Irishman, a court regular

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter is kept
to implicate is to fold something in, so one word wraps around another

blocks.note: Venus is the evening star
the first letter of witness
taken as written
Liam is an Irish first name; stuttering repeats its first letter

explanation.surface: The star witness at a trial drags a stammering Irishman into the case in court.
explanation.walkthrough: The courtroom setting sends you towards law, but the court is a tennis court; a stutter doubles the L of Liam.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus Williams is an American tennis champion who has played on court for decades, so she is a regular there.

clue.text: Former MP, otherwise ‘The Tory Slayer’?

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged in another way, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, all thirteen letters

explanation.surface: A former MP known by the nickname The Tory Slayer.
explanation.walkthrough: Roy Hattersley was a Labour MP and deputy party leader, so the nickname the letters spell out suits a political opponent of the Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: He sat in the House of Commons for Birmingham Sparkbrook until 1997 before entering the Lords, so he is a past member of Parliament.

clue.text: Rings numbers in manual regularly — India?

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
one thing in another sits inside it, so these letters go within the kept ones

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of manual
N is short for number, doubled for the plural
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A question about ringing numbers in a phone manual for India.
explanation.walkthrough: The kept letters of the manual take in the doubled N, then India's letter goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Annuli is the Latin plural of annulus, a technical word for a ring shape, such as the band between two circles.

clue.text: Storage space restricts hospital, needing extra in passing

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so one word holds another inside it

blocks.note: a byte is a unit of computer storage
H is the abbreviation for hospital
in cricket a bye is an extra, a run scored without the ball hitting the bat

explanation.surface: A lack of storage space limits a hospital, which needs more room along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket scores runs not credited to the batter as extras, and a bye is one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom used to introduce an incidental remark, meaning incidentally or mentioned casually along the way.

clue.text: Creature backtracking in jungle

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the letters lie inside the next word
backtracking is going back over your route, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the middle letters of jungle, read backwards

explanation.surface: An animal retracing its steps through the jungle.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the three central letters of jungle from right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnu, also called a wildebeest, is a large African antelope, so it is an animal or creature.

clue.text: Tree over edge of pavement leading to parent’s complaint

indicators.note: an edge is the very end of something, so the final letter is kept
to lie over something is to cover it, so one word wraps around a letter

blocks.note: the ash is a common tree
the last letter of pavement
MA is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A tree overhanging the kerb gives a parent something to complain about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parent's complaint' reads as a grumble, but the possessive belongs to the wordplay piece and complaint alone is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint is a general word for a medical condition or ailment, and asthma is a chronic breathing disorder, an example of one.

clue.text: What a surprise to be entertained by artist resident on island

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is taken in, so one word goes inside another

blocks.note: ah is an exclamation of surprise
Titian was a Venetian Renaissance painter

explanation.surface: It is a great surprise to be hosted by an artist who lives on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What a surprise' is a whole exclamation standing for a two-letter one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tahitian is a person who lives on Tahiti, the largest island of French Polynesia in the Pacific.

clue.text: The writer intends to hurt

definitions.note: ILL is a noun here, meaning harm

blocks.note: the setter speaking of themself
the contraction of will

explanation.surface: The author means to cause harm.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer is I, and I'll is how the writer would say 'I intend to'; drop the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, ill means harm or injury, as in wishing someone ill, which matches hurt in its noun sense.

clue.text: One invents material in America stifling scientist that’s gutted

indicators.note: a gutted thing has had its insides removed, so only the outside letters stay
to stifle is to smother, so one word closes around another

blocks.note: the American spelling of fibre
the first and last letters of scientist

explanation.surface: An American inventor of fabric smothers a scientist who has been gutted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One invents material' looks like a textile designer; the definition is only 'One invents', someone who makes things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A fibster tells small lies, fibs, so they are a person who makes up stories rather than telling the truth.

clue.text: Appreciated new belt

blocks.note: ta is informal British for thanks, an expression of appreciation
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone is grateful for a new belt.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta is British slang for thank you; belt is a verb, to hit, not something worn.
explanation.definitionFit: To tan someone, or tan their hide, is an idiom for giving them a beating, the same as belting them.

clue.text: Sort of stick around withdrawing until there’s merriment

indicators.note: withdrawing is pulling back, so the letters run the other way
around means on every side, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: a joystick is a sort of stick
till means until

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stay around and not leave until the fun starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of stick' asks for a word that goes before stick, as joy does in joystick.
explanation.definitionFit: Jollity is cheerful high spirits and fun, which is a close synonym for merriment.

clue.text: Work with Parisian in dance music recording like this once?

blocks.note: OP is short for opus, a work
en is French for in
a reel is a lively Scottish dance and its tune

explanation.surface: A piece of music combined with a Parisian dance tune, recorded the old-fashioned way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian in' is the French word for in; the question mark flags that the definition describes old recording technology.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-reel tape, also called reel-to-reel, was the standard format for studio recording before cassettes and digital media.

clue.text: Position in commentary following length and line

indicators.note: commentary is spoken aloud, so the word is given by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for length
attitude is a position or stance, and sounds as if spelt with one T

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator discusses a bowler's line and length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line and length' is a cricket phrase for a bowler's accuracy, which makes 'Position' look like the definition; it is the sound-alike, and the definition is 'line'.
explanation.definitionFit: A latitude is an imaginary circle drawn on the globe parallel to the equator, one of the lines on a map.

clue.text: Fancy casserole? It’s right in the middle, tough on the outside

indicators.note: something in the middle is set at the centre, so a letter goes inside the word
the outside of a word is its two ends, so only those letters are kept

blocks.note: a casserole is a stew
R is the abbreviation for right
the first and last letters of tough

explanation.surface: A posh casserole is fine in the centre but tough at the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective for the casserole, but it is the exclamation 'Fancy!', as in 'Fancy that!'
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise; strewth is an old oath, a contraction of God's truth, much used in Australia.

clue.text: Political policy, something usually transparent, gathering no end of support

indicators.note: a gathering draws things together and holds them, so one piece surrounds another
the end of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: glass is usually see-through
taken as written
the last letter of support

explanation.surface: A political policy meant to be transparent attracts no support in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of support' tempts you to read 'lots of support', but 'no' goes inside and only the last letter of support follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasnost, Russian for openness, was Gorbachev's Soviet programme of greater government transparency in the 1980s.

clue.text: Feel embarrassed, lacking money and energy to attend lady

indicators.note: lacking something means being without it, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: to squirm is to wriggle with embarrassment
M is the abbreviation for money, removed
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A penniless man feels awkward and lacks the energy to escort a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking money and energy' looks like both are removed, but only money goes and energy is added.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to squire means to escort or accompany a woman, as a knight's attendant once did.

clue.text: Eighth time delving into old pothole

indicators.note: to delve into something is to dig inside it, so one letter goes within a word

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
T is the abbreviation for time
a pothole is a deep natural cave

explanation.surface: For the eighth time someone digs into an old hole in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: A pothole is a hole in a road, but it is also a vertical cave that potholers explore.
explanation.definitionFit: An octave is the interval of eight notes in a scale, and also the eighth day after a church festival.

clue.text: With pressure, obtain earlier, final slice off cake

indicators.note: a final slice taken off removes the very end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: ex means former or earlier
a torte is a rich layered cake

explanation.surface: Under pressure, someone gets the last slice of cake removed ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is split by a comma at the start: 'With pressure, obtain' is to get by force.
explanation.definitionFit: To extort is to get money or something else by threats or force, obtaining it through pressure.

clue.text: Control game with knight

blocks.note: RU is rugby union
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: Taking charge of a chess game using the knight.
explanation.walkthrough: Chess notation uses N for the knight because K is taken by the king.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a business or organisation is to manage or be in charge of it, the same as controlling it.

clue.text: In stand, fit dry bread

indicators.note: in means inside, so the following pieces go within the outer word

blocks.note: to be, as in 'let it be' or 'let it stand'
an ague is a fit of fever and shivering
TT means teetotal, off alcohol

explanation.surface: A display stand holds suitable dry loaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Fit is a noun, a sudden attack of illness, and dry means not drinking alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A baguette is a long thin French loaf with a crisp crust, a particular kind of bread.

clue.text: Decorate bathroom again? Cream right for makeover

indicators.note: a makeover remodels something completely, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the cream is the best, the elite
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Redoing the bathroom with a cream colour for a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: Cream looks like a paint colour for the bathroom, but it means the best.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiles are the usual wall covering in a bathroom, so tiling it afresh is one way of redecorating, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Annual feast youths served excitedly across area

indicators.note: doing something excitedly is agitated and jumbled, so the letters are mixed up
stretching across something spans it, so the jumbled letters go either side

blocks.note: the fodder, twelve letters
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Young people eagerly serve food at an annual feast across the district.
explanation.walkthrough: The youths serving at a feast fit the picture, which hides that their letters are the raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrove Tuesday, Pancake Day in Britain, is the day before Lent begins, traditionally marked by feasting before the fast.
